commits.author: Marco Andronaco
commits.subject: perf: stop re-rendering the message list on every composer keystroke
commits.body:
App is one large component, so typing into the composer (a useState
on App itself) re-ran the render for the entire tree, including
recomputing action-group summaries and O(n*m) diffs for every tool
call in every message on each keystroke.

Extract the message list into a memoized MessagesPane and give its
callback props (scroll handler, question-resolved handler) stable
identities via useCallback, so it only re-renders when the actual
message/session data changes.

commits.author: Marco Andronaco
commits.subject: perf: don't re-render every message on each streamed token
commits.body:
renderedMessages previously created a brand-new wrapper object for
every message on every render, even for messages the stream update
didn't touch (applyStreamedPartUpdate/applyStreamedPartDelta already
keep untouched messages referentially stable). That defeated any
possible per-message memoization, so each streamed token re-ran
timeline building and diffing for the whole conversation, not just
the message actually being typed into.

Cache the wrapper per underlying message object (WeakMap) so unrelated
messages keep the same reference, and extract the per-message render
into a memoized MessageArticle that skips re-rendering unless its
message actually changed.

commits.author: Marco Andronaco
commits.subject: perf: skip unchanged messages on periodic refresh, stabilize remark plugins
commits.body:
mergeFetchedMessages always returned a fresh object per message on
every 3.5s poll, even when nothing about that message actually
changed content-wise, wiping out the WeakMap/memo caching added
earlier for the entire conversation each poll. Reuse the previous
message reference when the merged parts are logically equal.

Also hoist ReactMarkdown's remarkPlugins array to a module constant
instead of a new array literal on every render, since a changing
plugins reference makes it more likely react-markdown treats it as a
config change and redoes pipeline setup work on every streamed token.

commits.author: Marco Andronaco
commits.subject: perf: skip the 3.5s polling fallback while live updates are connected
commits.body:
The session/message poll and the SSE event stream were both running
unconditionally: every session./message./todo./question. event
already triggers a debounced refreshSessions+loadSelected via
scheduleRefresh, on top of the incremental part deltas applied
directly to state. The separate setInterval fired every 3.5s
regardless, doing a second full refetch+merge of the whole message
list during active streaming for no benefit.

Track eventStreamState in a ref and skip the interval's refetch while
it reads "live" — the poll now only does anything when the stream
isn't actually connected, which is what it's a fallback for.

commits.subject: Release hardening, rename to Harness Remote, and PR review preparation
commits.body:
### Release pipeline hardening
- APK workflow triggers on both main and v* tags
- Web regression tests (i18n, UI, settings, model, events) run in CI before Android packaging
- Bridge test suite runs in CI before Android packaging
- Fixed YAML syntax for apksigner step (multi-line run: |)
- AAB workflow uses npm run cap:sync:android (includes native LiveEventsPlugin)
- AAB artifact renamed from opencode-remote-aab-* to harness-remote-aab-*

### Rename to Harness Remote
- Bridge package renamed to harness-remote-omp (name, bin, usage string, clientInfo)
- README: updated download URL, technology stack references
- In-app help link corrected from gervaso-assistant/opencode-remote-android to giuliastro/harness-remote
- Regression test validates the canonical repository link and rejects the old owner
Old localStorage keys kept for backward compatibility

### Documentation
- README: expanded OMP bridge setup with prerequisites, step-by-step app config, curl verification, and security guidance
- README: updated CI section to reflect tag-triggered releases and signing requirements
- OMP-INTEGRATION-PLAN.md: added release gate section with acceptance criteria

### OMP session stability (existing work)
- Snapshot persistence separated from live streaming; polling no longer forces session/load
- Explicit refresh on session open; identical updates skip React state replacement
- Auto-scroll only for new content appended while at the bottom

commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix(bridge): correct OMP history, titles, and directory matching
commits.body:
Verified against OMP 17.1.3, which behaves differently from the test doubles
in three ways:

- OMP never echoes the submitted prompt, so the acknowledgement recorded for
  deduplication survived the turn and swallowed the persisted user message on
  the first history replay. Acknowledgements now apply only to live echoes.
- OMP session listings carry no title, so every session was shown as "Mobile
  session". Titles now come from the creation title, then the first prompt,
  then a short session id.
- Session listings compared directories as exact strings while session
  creation normalised them, so a directory written with forward slashes
  matched nothing on Windows.

Agent-initiated ACP requests were routed to the pending-response map and
silently dropped; an unanswered one would stall the agent until the prompt
timeout, so they now receive a JSON-RPC error. Adds --cors, without which the
documented browser mode cannot reach the bridge at all, and corrects the
README claim that --root limits the agent's filesystem access: it bounds the
bridge's own endpoints, not OMP, which approves its own tool calls.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix: recover from an unbootable saved server configuration
commits.body:
Typing a host such as http://192.168.1.64 one character at a time passes
through http: and http://, both of which produce an unparseable base URL.
streamURL threw inside a render effect, React unmounted the tree, and autosave
had already persisted the half-typed host, so every later launch reproduced the
empty root. On Android that is a black screen with no way out but clearing the
app data.

Connection guards now share isValidServerConfig, autosave refuses an incomplete
draft rather than persisting a crash, and an ErrorBoundary turns any remaining
failure into a screen that can reset the saved server settings. The new
test:config suite covers the exact typing sequence and runs in both workflows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat: explain what the host field accepts
commits.body:
The placeholder offered an IP, a bare name and an https URL without saying
which to prefer, so a failing Windows computer name read as "the scheme is
missing" and led to typing http:// by hand. Windows announces its name over
NetBIOS/LLMNR, which phones do not implement, and routers rarely publish DHCP
hostnames in DNS, so a bare computer name usually cannot be resolved at all.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.body:
The README described a two-backend app rather than a harness-agnostic one, so
adding a harness read as an exception. States the supported set in one table
with PI listed as planned, and says what adding a harness involves. Also drops
the last product-name leftover in the LICENSE.

 # Harness Remote
 
-Harness Remote is a companion app for controlling supported coding-agent backends—currently OpenCode and OMP—from phone or desktop, even when you are not at your main workstation.
+Harness Remote is a companion app for controlling coding-agent harnesses from phone or desktop, even when you are not at your main workstation.
 It is designed to make daily usage simple: connect to a backend, check active sessions, see progress, send new prompts or slash commands, and stop a running action when supported.
 
-> **Note for AI/harness systems**: This repository is self-documenting. To configure a supported backend and the app autonomously, point your AI assistant to this repository URL (`https://github.com/giuliastro/harness-remote`) or this README and ask it to set up Harness Remote.
+## Supported Harnesses
+
+The app is backend-agnostic: you pick the harness in **Settings** and each one keeps its own saved connection, so you can switch between them without re-entering anything.
+
+| Harness | Status | How it connects |
+|---|---|---|
+| [OpenCode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) | supported | directly to the OpenCode HTTP server |
+| Oh My Pi (OMP) | supported | through the local bridge included in this repository |
+| PI | planned | — |
+
+Support levels differ by what each harness exposes. The [OpenCode](#opencode-server-setup) and [OMP](#oh-my-pi-bridge-setup) sections below document the setup and the per-backend limitations.
+
